source.title: Rapid Convergence of the Unadjusted Langevin Algorithm: Isoperimetry Suffices

checks.paper_location: Official proceedings main PDF and supplemental archive
checks.claim: The official supplement contains the complete 29-page camera-ready PDF, including Appendices B.2.1 and B.2.2.
checks.note: The archive member is langevin_neurips_camera_ready.pdf. Appendix pages 16-19 were inspected and agree with the author-hosted full version at https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/wibisono/VW19.pdf. The official supplement is a ZIP, not a standalone Supplemental.pdf.

checks.claim: The LSI normalization is \(2\alpha H_\nu(\rho)\le J_\nu(\rho)\).
checks.note: The code uses actual extended KL and the squared relative score. For normalized \(\rho=r\nu\), KL is identified with \(\int r\log r\,d\nu\). The endpoint retains separate finiteness proofs; the total real-conversion aliases alone do not express finiteness.

checks.claim: The functional inequality applies to density tests.
checks.note: IsLogSobolev tests strictly positive \(C^1\) relative probability densities. Its normalization matches the source, but equivalence with the full smooth-function formulation and extension by approximation are not proved. The endpoint supplies paths in this restricted class explicitly.

checks.paper_location: Section 3, equation (11); Appendix B.2.1, equations (28)-(29), pages 5 and 17
checks.note: The actual measure update is the pushforward of the independent product of the current law and stdGaussian. Zero-time and step-endpoint identities are proved, with \(n=\operatorname{finrank}_{\mathbb R}E\). This identifies marginal laws; it does not construct the interpolation density or its weak equation.

The proof checks the standard Gaussian second moment, zero mean, independent-product cross-term cancellation, and square integrability. It requires a finite squared-gradient moment, not a second moment of \(X_0\). Dimension zero is included.

checks.paper_location: Appendix B.2.1, entropy calculation preceding equation (32), page 18
checks.claim: Density differentiation and integration by parts produce the entropy derivative.
checks.note: The derivative is derived from LocalEntropyRegularity, rather than assumed by the stronger wrapper. These data explicitly require local domination, integrability, measurability, and pointwise time derivatives. Constructing them for the actual frozen-drift densities remains open. They currently require a two-sided time neighborhood, including at zero.

checks.claim: The frozen-drift equation determines entropy production.
checks.note: The code proves the score identities and tests an admissible forced weak equation with \(\log r+1\). That weak equation is an input for all \(C^1\) tests with the displayed integrable terms. Its validity for the actual law, including this noncompact entropy test, is not inferred from compact-test identities.

checks.claim: Young's inequality leaves the Fisher coefficient \(-3/4\).
checks.note: The weighted cross term is proved integrable from its measurability and the two energy integrals. The estimate is \(H'\le-3J/4+\mathcal E\), with the same sign and coefficient as the source.

checks.paper_location: Appendix B.2.1, equation (33) and its following displacement calculation, pages 18-19
checks.claim: The joint gradient-error energy is bounded by \(L^2\) times displacement energy.
checks.note: frozen_gradient_error_energy proves integrability and the bound \(L^2(t^2G_0+2tn)\) on the actual independent product law. No drift-error estimate is assumed by that lemma.

checks.claim: The entropy cross term can be evaluated under the joint law of \(X_0\) and \(X_t\).
checks.note: The source rewrites the cross term directly as a joint expectation before applying Young. The current wrapper instead accepts a state-dependent error field and its energy bound. Connecting that field to the joint Gaussian discrepancy still needs conditional-mean identification and Jensen's inequality, or a direct joint-law weak-equation argument.

The shared theorem integral_norm_sq_gradient_gibbs_le proves this target bound under differentiability, gradient Lipschitzness, and a finite partition. Its proof uses translation invariance and a sub-Gaussian score estimate, rather than the source's Hessian and integration-by-parts argument. memLp_gradient_gibbsMeasure supplies square integrability. These results are not yet assembled with transport to discharge the LSI endpoint's hgradient input.

The endpoint retains this bound as hgradient, with an actual squared-gradient integral and an explicit integrability guard. Shared GibbsScore.lean already supplies the target moment and square integrability under differentiability, gradient Lipschitzness, and finite partition. The LSI endpoint does not connect that result with LSI-to-Talagrand and the coupling argument to derive hgradient.

checks.paper_location: Section 3.1, Lemma 3 and Theorem 2; end of Appendix B.2.1 and Appendix B.2.2, pages 6 and 19
checks.note: The displayed step restriction matches. The code additionally exposes \(\alpha\le L\) as hαL and requires positive \(L\). The appendix uses \(\alpha\le L\) to justify auxiliary small-step bounds but does not give a derivation there. Its derivation is not exported by the Lean development.

checks.paper_location: Section 3.1, Lemma 3, equation (12); Appendix B.2.1, final scalar calculation, pages 6 and 19
checks.note: The conclusion and step constants match. Lean sets \(A=(4L^2/\alpha)H(0)+2nL\) and obtains uniform forcing \(b=(\alpha/4)H(0)+(5/2)hnL^2\). Exact affine comparison with \(a=3\alpha/2\), \((1-e^{-ah})/a\le h\), and \(e^{-3x/2}+x/4\le e^{-x}\), where \(x=\alpha h\), give the stronger noise coefficient \(5/2\) before relaxing it to \(6\). The source instead uses a \(3hnL^2\) forcing term, an integrating factor, \(e^c\le1+2c\), and multiplicative exponential absorption.

checks.paper_location: Appendix B.2.2, first displayed bound, page 19
checks.note: The scalar recurrence is iterated using the existing affine recurrence lemmas. The exact helper also retains the finite-horizon factor \(1-e^{-\alpha hk}\). The final constant \(8\) follows from \(1-e^{-x}\ge3x/4\) for \(0\le x\le1/4\). Lean proves that denominator estimate from \(e^x\ge1+x\) and a reciprocal bound.

checks.claim: The published conclusion concerns the actual ULA laws.
checks.note: The endpoint concerns actual Gaussian ULA laws and actual KL; it does not assume the discrete recurrence. It requires a differentiable potential, gradient Lipschitzness, LSI, \(\alpha\le L\), density-law identification, and the displayed remaining analytic inputs. The stronger wrapper derives finite KL/Fisher, entropy continuity, its derivative, and production from local density data and an admissible weak equation. This is not yet Theorem 2 from only LSI and smoothness.

checks.paper_location: Sections 2.1 and 3.1; Theorem 2 and Appendix B.2.2, pages 3, 6 and 19
checks.claim: Gaussian initialization is an example; the theorem also states an accuracy threshold.
checks.note: The initial law is an arbitrary probability law satisfying the explicit path and moment assumptions; it is not required to be Gaussian. Finite initial KL follows from the identified density at time zero. The separate logarithmic iteration threshold for a requested \(\delta\), and the stationary-bias corollary, are not exported as LSI theorems.

checks.paper_location: Section 2.3.1, Theorem 1; Appendix B.1.3, pages 5 and 16
checks.claim: Continuous Langevin entropy decays at rate \(2\alpha\).
checks.note: The continuous-time comparison uses \(e^{-2\alpha t}\), distinct from the discrete factor \(e^{-\alpha hk}\). EntropyFlow derives actual-KL decay given an admissible density path and an explicit dissipation identity; it does not construct a Langevin SDE law or prove Talagrand's inequality.

verdict: The formalized normalization, Gaussian update, displacement and joint error estimates, one-step constant 6, and iterated constant 8 agree with the 2019 reference. The scalar one-step argument is a valid documented variant of Appendix B.2.1. The actual-law endpoint remains conditional: the code does not yet prove the complete published theorem from LSI and smoothness alone.
